Lynn buckles forward over her desk coughing; nearby candidates stop writing and turn to stare. By the end she is folded flat over the paper with the whole row watching her.
Lynn doubles over her desk in the library exam hall, then rises in tears as the proctor grips her arm and walks her out. The last shot leaves the proctor alone in the aisle, Lynn gone.

A young man in a striped polo strides through a printing plant past the presses, a young woman in a blue work uniform trailing him. He breaks into a hurry, and the shop's printer in a cream polo turns to face them.
Cut to the exam building corridor: a hand fills a paper cup at the water cooler, black boots planted at the counter, then an overhead shows the woman slumped against the wall beside the cooler.
The printer talks straight at the pair; the young woman in blue grins beside the man in the striped polo. The moment breaks on a cutaway to the same black boots striding away down the carpet.
Back in the plant, the printer keeps talking, eyes widening; the reverse holds on the couple listening, her smile fading as he goes on.
The printer pulls back and shakes a loose sheaf of pages at them. The young man answers; by the last shot both have gone quiet and still, watching him.

Lynn, bag on her shoulder, hurries out along the timber corridor glancing back. A suited man rushes past the doors, the camera whips to a blank wall, and it settles on an old monitor showing a figure at a cabinet.
Close on the printer mid-sentence in the plant, then he steps forward and puts a hand out across the frame towards the pair.
In the print shop Pat stares down at something in his hands; an insert catches his and Grace's hands at the bench. By the last shot she has stepped in beside him and both are reading the same page.
A long held take of the exam hall: an invigilator in a black suit paces between desks of writing candidates. Cut to the print shop, where the man in the striped polo stops working and looks up.
Someone bolts down the wood-panelled corridor past the stairwell; an overhead shot swings across the empty atrium below. The cut back finds Pat and Grace frozen, now both staring straight ahead.
Lynn hurries up the staircase with her backpack while a suited man crosses the lobby gates with a phone to his ear. She stops on the landing and turns back toward the stairs she just climbed.
The suited man shoves through a door at the stairwell; Lynn, sweating, glances back over her shoulder. The moment ends on the stairwell empty, both of them gone from frame.
Lynn shoulders an exterior door open into the daylit courtyard, doubles over on the ramp to catch her breath, then straightens up walking and pulls out her phone to read it.
A whip pan across the bike racks and courtyard; Lynn hurries past a yellow WATER column, checking behind her. The last shot opens out wide and leaves only a distant figure crossing the empty square.
Back in the darkened press hall a man walks out from between the machines past stacked paper; Pat watches, tense. An insert shows Grace's hand slipping from his as he opens his fingers.
A young man in a navy polo strides across the dim press floor, and the shot cuts to the man in the striped polo in the lit room, now gesturing off-screen as he talks.
A close insert of Lynn's hand tapping a travel card on a station reader, then she comes through the fare gates into the concourse and keeps walking under the station signage.
Lynn pushes out through the station fare gates, phone in hand, and heads away down a tunnel corridor; brief cuts to a phone waiting on a glass table and a blurred pass of two figures elsewhere.
A man in a dark suit scans the concourse. Lynn looks back over her shoulder, then twists her hair up into a knot as she keeps walking; by the end the suited man has pushed past, still searching.
Hair down, Lynn walks on thumbing a coded 'speech transcript' message into her phone; the alert then lands on a phone lying on cardboard, and a tearful woman faces a man in glasses in a print room.
Lynn whips round and keeps typing as she passes the Way Out signs; intercut, the woman in the blue uniform and the man in glasses go on talking until a second alert lights the phone on the cardboard.
In the print room the man in glasses drops his eyes while the woman in the blue uniform breaks down crying; it ends on a wide of her and a young man in a brown striped shirt staring, stunned.
Lynn taps another block of numbers into the group chat and keeps moving through the crowded concourse, head down over the screen; the cut returns to the couple still frozen in the print room.
Print room: the young man in the brown shirt presses the man in the cream polo, who answers quietly, then stands and walks back among the presses while the couple watch him go.

Lynn drops to her knees on the station floor beside her phone, then hunches over it wide-eyed and hammers out another set of answers; by the last shot she is typing two-handed as commuters stream past.
In the dim print shop a phone lights up on the glass desk beside a laptop. An older man in a striped polo walks over, Pat's face drops, and the man slams both hands on the table, pinning the phone.
Pat lurches up from the desk at the older man, who holds his ground and stares him down through his glasses. By the last shot Pat has gone still, Grace watching tensely over his shoulder.
Lynn keeps moving through the station with the phone up; focus racks past her shoulder to the commuters behind her, then she turns straight into the lens, frowning, and picks up speed.
A blurred figure bolts past Grace's laptop and runs between the printing presses. The shot settles outside on the shop's upper windows, where the figure crosses behind the glass and disappears.

Pat argues face to face with a bespectacled customer in a blue polo among parked motorbikes; the camera lifts to a high angle over them, then widens to the print-shop gate where a crowd of students has massed.
On screen, "Lighting your way to better" is typed into Google and the results fill with Nelson Mandela speech transcripts; cut to Grace at the laptop, who breaks into a grin.

Pat presses his palms together begging the crowd at the gate, then shouts them down. A phone pings with a new message, a packed hall of students erupts, and Pat ends up ringed by them, all on their phones.

A man in a dark suit strides down the station corridor while hurrying legs cross the tiles. Lynn keeps typing, and the closing insert shows her answer strings already delivered in the "L,B(3)" thread.

Lynn hurries through a tiled subway corridor thumbing her phone; an insert shows a chat thread filling with coded answer strings, then the cut lands on an extreme close-up of a girl's eyes receiving them.

The other end of the pipeline: a barcode file being edited on a design screen, a hand clicking the mouse, the girl's eyes snapping wide, then a wide of the dim print workshop where one figure works alone at a laptop.
Lynn strides at the camera wiping her face, an insert shows thumbs typing a fresh answer block under messages already marked read, and she walks on with the phone lowered.
A busker plays a keyboard against the station wall; the camera pushes in on his hands, then whips to Lynn passing behind him, glancing back over her shoulder as she keeps moving.
A blurred handoff across a parked motorbike racks into focus as a man in a brown shirt pushes slips of paper into a packed rank of waiting motorcycle-taxi riders, who start pulling away.
Lynn climbs from the lower level, boards an escalator and rides up with her backpack and phone clutched to her chest; by the last shot her eyes are off the screen and fixed ahead.
A train noses into the platform and rushes past the camera; cut to Lynn on the escalator, head up, phone forgotten in her hand as she registers the sound.
A passenger steps aboard carriage N5207 while Lynn bolts down the escalator and sprints along the platform; by the last shot the doors are shut and the train is still.
Lynn stops at the closed door and stares up through the glass, holding there, then tilts her head to the window; the cut answers with a woman's face wide open in a scream.
Shot from behind her, the carriages slide away past Lynn until the platform is bare and other passengers stream by; she turns and walks off under the yellow Way out signs.
An empty escalator shaft, then Lynn rides up in the crowd, steps off at the top and crosses the concourse alone, head down, finally passing a lit perfume billboard.
A platform clock reads 11:19:43 above Lynn's head; she walks past a blue door, and an insert of her hands on the phone cuts to her face screwing up as she reads the screen.

A man in a dark suit comes down the escalator and strides through the station in low-angle shots, intercut with Lynn still frowning at her phone; by the last shot she has turned and is looking back, alarmed.
One held take in the print shop: Pat hurries across to Grace, hunched over a laptop in her blue uniform, and by the end of the shot he is crouched beside her holding his phone to the screen.
A whip-pan snaps back to the station. Lynn's hands work a cracked phone, the text box filling to 'C A', and she ends walking the platform with her frown deepening over the screen.
A wall clock reads 07:22; outside the exam centre students shout and clutch their heads, then a ringed hand twists a motorbike throttle and the bike blurs away out of frame.
A figure in a dark shirt climbs onto a bench and shoves a ceiling panel aside; the reverse angle from below shows only his legs as he hauls himself up into the roof.
The screen now reads 'C A B B'. Lynn grimaces over it and turns away into the dark, and by the last shot she has stopped dead on the empty platform, chin up, looking down the line.
Lynn reads the station: a 'Platform 12 / No Exit' sign, a blurred pan over the Redfern tiling, then she stands under the Sydenham board with her hair lifting before swinging away.
Lynn feeds a coin into a vending machine and jabs the keypad; the coil turns on a chocolate-chip cookie, and the moment ends on her face, eyes dropping, worn out.
Commuter legs hurry past as Lynn keeps thumbing answer strings into the cracked phone; a tear runs down her cheek, and by the last shot the chat has filled with sent letter codes.
In the print shop Pat grins at his phone, Grace builds an A-B-C-D barcode on a laptop, and Pat ends the run walking off between the presses with a roll of printed paper.

Lynn grabs a drink and a muffin from a station vending tray and tears into them, intercut with the press floor and with a suited man striding fast along the platform. She ends with her mouth crammed full.
Orange-vested motorbike couriers mass in a Thai yard while a man in a blue polo shouts and points them into line; intercut, Lynn drains the bottle. Ends low among the riders' legs and wheels.
Lynn chews and sweats on the near-empty Redfern platform; the grey-haired man in the suit bellows in close-up, and she turns and walks off down the platform past the vending machine.
On the press floor sheets are handed out to vested riders; Lynn trails her fingers along the tiled REDFERN letters until an older man's hand closes on her shoulder strap from behind and stops her.

A blurred scuffle leaves her orange backpack on the platform floor with the suited man standing over it. Lynn huddles at the wall cramming the last of the food into her mouth, then straightens to face him.

A scooter revs and a wall of couriers lights its headlights inside the printing house; Lynn stands stricken, a phone is raised over a seated man's shoulder, and the convoy finally pours out into the street.
The screen holds on black, then opens on a young man alone at a bare desk in a white room, writing, while a figure stands over him with a bag. His face is never clearly shown.

In a bright glass-walled hall a woman in a white blazer with a staff ID talks steadily at Lynn. Lynn answers nothing, staring up past her; across the long held take her jaw sets and her eyes go glassy.
Wide on the library stacks: Lynn sits in a row of chairs beside another student. Insert of a phone opening a beach photo of a smiling girl and boy; back on Lynn, her eyes have dropped to the floor.
Through a glass wall Lynn watches Bank sit alone at a bare table with his jacket and a snack. She lifts her eyes, then the shot drifts out of focus onto an empty door frame and blurred shelves.
Bank answers questions in the white-walled room while Lynn stands at the glass watching. He stays level; she begins fixed on him and ends with her head lowered, turning away from the glass.
Bank sits alone against a whiteboard, then the film cuts to Grace staring out a bright window. She brings up a beach selfie of herself and a boy on her phone and ends looking down at it, eyes wet.
An 'International Arrivals' sign at night, then Pat and Grace on the arrivals balcony holding up a glowing heart sign. By the last shot they are laughing, Grace fiddling with an orchid garland.
Lynn reaches them and Pat lifts the garland toward her. Grace and Pat beam, but Lynn stays flat-faced and starts talking back at them, unsmiling.
The three talk at the railing under the airport sign, Grace leaning in and laughing. On the reverse angle Pat holds the orchid garland out to Lynn and she still has not taken it.
Grace drops her eyes and says something to Lynn, whose back is to us. The camera then pushes to a tight over-shoulder on Lynn, who turns and holds Pat's gaze without smiling.

Lynn stands face to face with Pat in the airport hall, unmoved as he talks. The wider shot adds Grace, who reaches out to shake Lynn's hand; by the last frame Lynn has swept past both of them and out of shot, leaving the pair standing.

Alone, Lynn perches on her suitcase outside the glass doors, back to camera, framed by the doorway. The cut pulls out to the near-empty concourse, shrinking her to one small figure under the departure signs.

Her father walks up to her by the terminal doors. They square off in shot/reverse-shot, he talking with hands on his hips; Lynn's wary glance over her shoulder turns into a tight, cornered stare by the last frame.
Her father keeps speaking, calm and steady. The reverse stays on Lynn, and across the long take her held composure gives way: eyes reddening and brimming, mouth tightening, by the end close to tears.
In an airport arrivals hall Lynn's father pulls her into a hug and she breaks down sobbing on his shoulder; the last shot pulls back wide, the two still clinging together beside her suitcase.
Out of black, a vast empty white hall with Lynn alone on a chair in school uniform. The camera closes to her profile and she is mid-answer, calm, while a clerk types at a desk behind her.

Night party: hands fly up under gold balloons and confetti, Grace beams beside Pat, Pat swigs from a beer bottle, a boy screams along, and the run ends tight on their matching 'STIC 1460' score shirts.
Back in the bare hall, over Lynn's shoulder a figure in black questions her across the table; cut to her face and the composure is gone, her eyes drifting off to the side.
Night at home: her father watches a broadcast from his armchair while Lynn sits on the floor; by the next shot she has moved up onto the sofa, lounging and half-smiling as he talks behind her.

A LINE message from Pat says Bank has already taken his million and her share is waiting. Cut to Lynn staring dead ahead in the empty hall; back on the phone the thread ends with 'Lynn left the chat.'

Insert of a phone chat where Pat's thread ends with 'Lin left the chat', then cut away to a warm wood-panelled party: Pat turns and talks off-screen, and the reverse lands on Grace smiling back at him.
Close-up of hands kneading a bare leg, then the camera pulls back past a table of empty bottles to Pat and Grace sprawled together on the couch, the massage over and both slumped in the mess.
Back to Lynn alone in the white hall, holding the camera's gaze through a long take; by the end of the shot she has dropped her eyes to the floor and stopped speaking.

In a dim office a woman in a black blazer sits behind a desk facing two people shot from behind; the scene cuts to a clipboard close-up of a school-crested letter already carrying a handwritten signature.
A congratulatory scholarship banner with Bank's portrait hangs on a school wall; cut inside to Bank himself hunched over a desk in a blue-lit classroom, writing hard, head down.

A fast run of near-black shots in a cramped cluttered laundry room: a figure hauls a bucket past the doorway, glimpses of someone working among hanging cloth, the frames darkening until the picture goes fully black.

Lynn walks out along the bright school corridor as other students drift away down it. Cut to her phone in hand: a chat message from Bank, so she ends the moment stopped over the screen instead of walking.

Night: Lynn stands in the street outside a lit laundry shop with a scooter parked in its doorway. A crumpled white school shirt scrawled in red and black lies on the tiles; by the last shot she is standing over it, head lowered.

The shop has been rebuilt: a new "Mister Bank" wash-dry-iron sign, then rows of brand-new washing machines still sealed in bubble wrap. Lynn takes it in, and the last shot leaves her small behind the glass, inside the new place.

A wooden door opens onto the back workshop, where Bank waits leaning against a bench with his arms folded. Lynn stops in the doorway and stays there, talking across the room without closing the distance.
Shot/reverse across the workshop: Bank stares back flat and unmoving while Lynn speaks. By the last shot she has stopped talking and her eyes have slid away from him.
Bank faces Lynn in the dim laundry while she sits against the wooden door, watching him without moving. By the last shot he has dropped his eyes to the floor.
Lynn frowns at him across the room; Bank's face snaps open in shock, mouth parted, then settles back into a flat stare while she keeps her eyes on him.
Lynn stares in silence, then Bank holds out a yellow leaflet to her, caught in close insert. The framing widens to an over-shoulder two-shot with him facing her squarely and the paper gone from view.
The coverage tightens to warm sunlit profiles, Lynn then Bank. An insert catches the yellow leaflet in mid-air above his outstretched arm, and the moment ends on Lynn in profile, eyes lowered.

In a dim room Bank talks in tight profile while Lynn listens, facing away from him. Over the exchange her jaw tightens and her eyes go glassy; by the last shot she is near tears and still has not looked at him.
Bank drops his gaze to the floor as he keeps speaking, then the camera holds on Lynn alone; her stare hardens and her mouth sets as she takes in what he said.
Bank, still in profile, looks off past her; a cutaway to the glass-panelled door and a hanging umbrella, then he turns square to camera and speaks straight at Lynn, no longer avoiding her.
Lynn stands at the door with her back to him, then turns her head to look back, face drawn. An insert of a hand closing on the doorknob ends the beat - she is leaving.
Lynn's hand closes on the door handle of the dim laundry while Bank argues at her from behind. She keeps her back turned, but by the last shot she has stopped and stands in profile, not leaving.
Cut to Lynn against a blank white wall, eyes shut. A beat on Bank's face in the dark laundry, then back to Lynn with her eyes open, staring flatly into the lens.
In a washed-out white corridor Lynn's father sits beside her with his head bowed and eyes lowered. She turns off to the side in profile, face tight and close to tears.
Her father lifts his head and gives her a small smile. The camera then pulls back to a wide of the empty white corridor, the two of them alone on chairs at the far end.
Back in the dark laundry: Bank talks on in profile, chin up, while Lynn stands backlit and still. He turns to face her directly, and the moment ends back on her hand resting on the door handle.
In the dim room Lynn holds a tight, troubled close-up with Bank blurred behind her; by the end she has crossed to the wooden door, turned back for one last look, and is on her way out.
Shot from behind, Lynn is walked through a bare white room past men in suits toward a camcorder standing on a tripod, which the frame settles on.
Two statements straight to camera: Bank speaking in the dim room, then a cut to Lynn's father against a blank white wall, the setting flipping from shadow to clinical light.
Lynn sits across a white table from a suited man while the camcorder records; by the shot's end she has turned her back to him, facing away in her chair.
